newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea shipping more metal stocks abroad - traders.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea shipping more metal stocks abroad - traders.

text.p: South Korea's lagging metal demand, hit by a continued economic slowdown, has forced local metal houses to increasingly ship stocks overseas to cut carrying costs, traders in Seoul said on Thursday.
"Recent failures of several domestic companies involved in the metal sector have dampened both demand and trade," a trader with a major trading firm said.

Earlier on Thursday LG Metals Corp said that it had sold about 10,000 tonnes of copper supplied by Chile's Codelco to European metal firm Metallgesellschaft and that the cargo would be shipped to Singapore.
Traders said LG Metals, South Korea's largest copper producer, had also sold about 5,000 tonnes of copper to another European merchant in May.
The 5,000 tonne deal has not been confirmed by LG.
Traders estimate South Korea's copper and copper product exports surged 53.4 percent to 74,257 tonnes for the first four months of this year from 48,408 tonnes a year earlier.
They also estimate aluminium and aluminium product exports jumped 67.1 percent to 91,400 tonnes from 54,508 tonnes.
On Thursday aluminium import premiums for spot delivery were unchanged from the previous week at $95-$100 a tonne CIF Pusan over LME's cash prices, traders said.
They said domestic aluminium prices were expected to fall this week to 1,520,000 won a tonne from 1,550,000-1,560,000 won a week ago.
Domestic copper and zinc prices were flat at 2,467,000 won and 1,348,000 won a tonne, respectively.
South Korea's Office of Supply on Tuesday bought through tenders 2,245 tonnes of aluminium ingot at $1,520,000 won a tonne from LG Metals.
